s1003.content:
Romanus left his home at thirty-five, carrying a copy of the Lives of the Fathers of the desert, and went to live as a hermit in the forests of the Jura mountains, between today’s France and Switzerland. His younger brother St. Lupicinus followed him, and so many came that they founded monasteries, among them Condat, around which the town of Saint-Claude later grew.

The two brothers governed their monks together, Romanus with gentleness and Lupicinus with strictness. They are called the fathers of the Jura, the desert fathers of Gaul. Their sister led a monastery of women nearby.
s1003.intercession: St. Romanus, pray for us, and for all who suffer in mind. Amen.

s1004.content:
Bruno was a Saxon noble and a chaplain at the court of the young Emperor Otto III. Moved by the martyrdom of St. Adalbert of Prague, he became a Camaldolese monk under St. Romuald, and was consecrated a missionary archbishop for the peoples of the east.

He preached among the Hungarians and the pagan Pechenegs of the steppes, and wrote a life of St. Adalbert. In 1009 he went to the Prussians, near the borders of Lithuania, and was killed there with eighteen companions. He is called the second apostle of the Prussians.
s1004.intercession: St. Bruno, pray for us, and for all who carry the Gospel into danger. Amen.

s1005.content:
Dominic was a shepherd boy of Navarre in Spain who became a monk. When he refused to hand over the goods of his monastery to the king of Navarre, he was driven out, and the king of Castile gave him the ruined abbey of Silos.

He rebuilt it in 1041, made it a great center of learning, art, and prayer, and gave its riches to ransom Christians held captive by the Moors. A century later, a noblewoman who prayed at his tomb for a child gave birth to a son and named him Dominic: St. Dominic de Guzmán, the founder of the Dominicans. The monks of Silos still sing there.
s1005.intercession: St. Dominic, pray for all captives and for all mothers awaiting a child. Amen.

s1006.content:
Stephen was a nobleman of Auvergne in France who, after time in Italy among hermits, returned to live alone in the woods of Muret, near Limoges, for nearly fifty years. Others came to share his life of poverty, silence, and prayer.

When asked what rule his followers lived by, he said that there is no rule but the Gospel of Christ. From his disciples came the Order of Grandmont, a strict order of hermits. He was canonized in 1189.
s1006.intercession: St. Stephen, pray for us, that the Gospel may be our only rule. Amen.

s1007.content:
Elizabeth Hesselblad was born into a Lutheran family in Sweden and went to America at eighteen to earn a living as a nurse. Caring for Catholic patients, she was drawn to the faith, and became a Catholic in 1902.

In Rome she lived in the house where St. Bridget of Sweden had died, and refounded the Order of the Most Holy Savior, the Bridgettines, as active sisters praying for Christian unity. During the Second World War she hid Jews in her convent in Rome, and she is honored as Righteous Among the Nations. She was canonized in 2016.
s1007.intercession: St. Elizabeth, pray for the unity of all Christians. Amen.

s1008.content:
Lodovico Pavoni was a priest of Brescia in Italy who opened a school where poor and abandoned boys could learn a trade, beginning with a printing press, so that they could earn an honest living; he also opened a school for deaf children.

In 1825 he founded the Sons of Mary Immaculate to carry on the work. In 1849, during the uprising of Brescia, he led his boys out of the city to safety in the hills, and died there of exhaustion. He was canonized in 2016.
s1008.intercession: St. Lodovico, pray for all young people who need a trade and a home. Amen.

s1009.content:
Józef Kowalski was a young Polish Salesian priest in Kraków, secretary to the head of his province, who worked with young people. He was arrested by the Gestapo in 1941 with other Salesians and sent to Auschwitz.

In the camp he heard confessions, prayed with the prisoners, and secretly said Mass. Ordered by a guard to trample his rosary, he refused, and he was beaten and drowned in a barrel of sewage in 1942. He was beatified in 1999 among the 108 Polish martyrs of the Second World War.
s1009.intercession: Bl. Józef, pray for us, that we may never let go of our faith. Amen.

s1010.content:
Hildegard Freund was born into a Jewish family in Germany and studied philosophy. Married and living in Berlin, she fell gravely ill in 1909 and recovered against all expectation; she saw it as a gift from God and became a Catholic.

In Vienna she gave her life to working women, especially home workers who were paid almost nothing, and in 1919 she became one of the first women elected to the Austrian parliament. She founded the sisterhood of Caritas Socialis to serve the poor, and raised a daughter. She was beatified in 2012.
s1010.intercession: Bl. Hildegard, pray for all who work for justice in public life. Amen.

s1011.content:
Miroslav Bulešić was a young priest of Istria, on the Adriatic, who renewed his parishes after the Second World War and spoke out against the Communist authorities who were persecuting the Church.

In August 1947, while he was accompanying the bishop for confirmations at Lanišće, a mob stormed the parish house, and he was stabbed and his throat was cut. He was twenty-seven. He had written that his revenge would be forgiveness. He was beatified in 2013.
s1011.intercession: Bl. Miroslav, pray for us, that our revenge may be forgiveness. Amen.

s1012.content:
Anton Durcovici was born in Austria and grew up in Romania, where he became a priest, a professor, and in 1947 bishop of Iași. He visited every parish of his diocese and preached tirelessly.

When the Communist regime tried to separate Romanian Catholics from Rome, he refused. He was arrested in 1949 and, after years of interrogation, died of hunger and cold in the prison of Sighet in 1951. He was beatified in 2014.
s1012.intercession: Bl. Anton, pray for all who are persecuted for their fidelity. Amen.

s1013.content:
Vladimir Ghika was a prince of a family that had ruled Moldavia and Wallachia, raised in the Orthodox Church in Romania and educated in France. He became a Catholic in 1902 and gave himself to works of charity, founding the first free hospital in Bucharest and serving the sick in war and epidemic.

He was ordained a priest in 1923, and was allowed to celebrate in both the Latin and Byzantine rites. When the Communists took power he stayed in Romania to serve; he was arrested in 1952 and died in Jilava prison in 1954, at eighty. He was beatified in 2013.
s1013.intercession: Bl. Vladimir, pray for us, and for the unity of East and West. Amen.

s1014.content:
Benigna was an orphan of Ceará in northeastern Brazil, raised by adoptive parents, who helped with the housework, went to Mass, and taught the catechism to other children.

When she was thirteen, a boy who had pursued her stopped her on her way to fetch water and tried to force himself on her. She refused, and he killed her with a machete. She was beatified in 2022, the first person of Ceará to be beatified.
s1014.intercession: Bl. Benigna, pray for all children, and protect them from harm. Amen.

s1015.content:
Antonio Rosmini was a priest and philosopher of northern Italy, one of the great Catholic thinkers of his century, a friend of the novelist Alessandro Manzoni. He founded the Institute of Charity, the Rosminians, ready to undertake any work of charity God asked of them.

In his book The Five Wounds of the Church he called for the renewal of the Church’s worship, the formation of its clergy, and its freedom, and for a time it was placed on the Index. He accepted the Church’s judgment in humility, and his thought was later recognized as faithful. He was beatified in 2007.
s1015.intercession: Bl. Antonio, pray for all who seek the truth. Amen.

s1016.content:
Lucien Botovasoa was a schoolteacher in southeastern Madagascar, married with eight children, who joined the Secular Franciscans and lived a life of prayer, fasting, and service.

During the uprising of 1947 he was arrested by a local leader who hated the Christians. Knowing he would be killed, he prayed for his people and forgave his executioners, asking God to have mercy on them, and he was beheaded. He was beatified in 2018, the first layman of Madagascar to be beatified as a martyr.
s1016.intercession: Bl. Lucien, pray for all teachers and fathers. Amen.

s1017.content:
Alfredo Cremonesi was an Italian priest of the Pontifical Institute for Foreign Missions who sailed to Burma in 1925, promising never to return home. He served the Karen people in the mountain villages for nearly thirty years, through war, Japanese occupation, and hunger.

In 1953, during fighting between government soldiers and rebels, he stayed with his people and was shot by soldiers in his village. He was beatified in 2019.
s1017.intercession: Bl. Alfredo, pray for all missionaries, and for the people of Myanmar. Amen.

s1018.content:
Nazaria March was born in Madrid and emigrated with her family to Mexico, where she joined the Little Sisters of the Abandoned Elderly, who sent her to Bolivia. There she cared for the old and poor for many years.

In 1925 she founded the Missionaries of the Crusade, sisters who work in the poorest places with the laity, especially women, in the service of the Church. She was the first woman of Bolivia to found a congregation. She died in Buenos Aires in 1943, and was canonized in 2018.
s1018.intercession: St. Nazaria, pray for all who serve the poor. Amen.

s1019.content:
Natalia Tułasiewicz was a teacher of Polish literature in Poznań and a leader in the Catholic lay apostolate. During the Second World War she volunteered to go into Germany among the Polish women taken there for forced labor, to support them and keep their faith alive.

She was arrested in 1944, tortured, and sent to the camp at Ravensbrück, where she was killed in the gas chamber on Good Friday in 1945. She was beatified in 1999 among the 108 Polish martyrs of the war.
s1019.intercession: Bl. Natalia, pray for all who suffer in captivity. Amen.

s1020.content:
Francesco Spinelli was a priest of Bergamo in Italy who, praying in the basilica of St. Mary Major in Rome, saw in his heart a community of women adoring Christ in the Eucharist day and night.

In 1882 he founded the Sisters Adorers of the Blessed Sacrament, who unite adoration with service to the poor and the disabled. He suffered failure, debt, and humiliation along the way, and bore them patiently. He was canonized in 2018.
s1020.intercession: St. Francesco, pray for us, that we may adore Christ in the Eucharist. Amen.
